task_description:
# Task for CellForge (Gene-Mila matched comparison)

Predict, for each perturbation listed in `heldout_perturbations.json`, the mean expression of every gene in
`cellforge_input.h5ad` (same genes, same order, same normalisation: counts per 10k, log1p) in K562 cells carrying
that CRISPR perturbation. None of these perturbations has any cell in the training file: this is the unseen-
perturbation setting. Train only on `cellforge_input.h5ad`; do not download or use any other copy of this screen.

Output: `predictions.npz` with `perts` (the held-out keys, as listed) and `means` (n_perts x n_genes, float).
Scored by Gene-Mila's evaluator: pearson_delta (correlation of predicted and true change from control, per
perturbation), MSE, and MSE/PCC/R2 on the top-20 DE genes.

PCA captures major expression axes (e.g., cell cycle, stress), and co-expression networks reflect functional gene modules.

Phase 3: Optional graph-based or autoencoder models; biological validation
Phase 4: Final model selection, reproducibility checks, and submission format validation
roadmap.timeline: Approximately 4-6 weeks: Phase 1 (1-2 weeks), Phase 2 (1-2 weeks), Phase 3 (1-2 weeks, optional), Phase 4 (1 week). Adjust based on compute and personnel.
milestones: M1: Metadata verified and QC report generated (end of week 1)
M2: Baseline models implemented and cross-validated (end of week 2)
M3: Best linear/shrinkage model selected with cross-validation performance (end of week 3-4)
M4: Biological validation of known essential genes completed (end of week 4-5)
M5: Final predictions generated, format checked, and submitted (end of week 6)

computational: Single machine with at least 32 GB RAM, multi-core CPU; optional GPU for secondary models
Python environment with anndata, scanpy, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn; optionally torch
Pinned software versions and deterministic seeds
biological: Access to literature on K562 CRISPRi effects and essential genes
Co-expression module derivation from control cells
Optional: external pathway annotations only if permitted
personnel: Data scientist/ML engineer for model development and validation
Biologist for biological validation and interpretation
Project manager for timeline and decision log maintenance
resources.decision_support_resources: No decision support provided; resources are estimated based on task complexity and standard requirements.

risks: Poor generalization to functionally isolated held-out perturbations
Noisy perturbation means due to low cell numbers
Format or normalization mismatch with evaluator
mitigation: Use shrinkage toward control and cross-validated regularization
Flag low-cell perturbations and apply strong shrinkage or exclusion
Include batch as covariate if confounded; avoid aggressive batch correction
Use leave-perturbation-out cross-validation and simple models
Implement automated format checks and dummy submission
Fix seeds, use deterministic solvers, and document software versions
contingency: If simple models fail to beat control baseline, fallback to control-mean with shrinkage
If biological validation fails for known essential genes, revisit feature construction and model assumptions
If computational resources are insufficient for secondary models, focus on linear/shrinkage models
risk_mitigation.decision_support_risk_mitigation: No decision support provided; risks and mitigations are identified from dataset analysis and baseline assessment.

performance: MSE and top-20 DE metrics on cross-validation
Stability of predictions across seeds (Pearson correlation > 0.95)
Calibration slope of true vs predicted delta
biological: Recovery of known essential gene knockdown signatures (e.g., ribosomal genes)
Enrichment of predicted top genes in relevant co-expression modules
Predicted effects for zero-baseline targets near control mean
technical: Format checks pass (keys, shapes, order, dtype)
Reproducibility: identical outputs on re-run with same seed
QC filtering does not remove entire perturbations
